children: Chile’s industrial production declined 5.1% year-on-year in July 2026, reversing a 1.3% increase in June.
The contraction was led by mining, which fell 7.2%, mainly due to a 10.7% decline in metal mining as copper extraction and processing dropped 9.4%.
The decline was attributed to unfavorable weather conditions in northern Chile that disrupted production, along with maintenance work at major mining operations.
Manufacturing output fell 4.9%, largely due to a 25.9% drop in coke and refined petroleum products, as weather-related disruptions affected gasoline and diesel production.
In contrast, utilities output increased 0.3%, supported by a 0.8% rise in electricity generation, particularly from hydroelectric plants.
On a monthly basis, industrial production fell 3.8%.

title: Chile Industrial Output Contracts in July
